title: Add the Stripe Customer Portal for cards, plan changes and cancellation
description: Owners open the portal from settings to update cards, change plans, download invoices and cancel.
acceptance_criteria:
- Only owners can open the portal
- Cancellation reflected in the app within a minute

title: Build the landing page, pricing page and sign-up
description: Marketing site at the root domain: what it does (with the receipt-reading demo), pricing, sign-up leading to Cognito and the trial, links to privacy, terms and support.
acceptance_criteria:
- Lighthouse 90+ for performance and accessibility
- Sign-up to first sheet in under 3 minutes

title: Process Stripe webhooks through SQS into team entitlements
description: Signature check, idempotency by event ID, SQS with a dead-letter queue, worker that fetches the latest subscription and updates plan, seats, status and period end. Served in both regions.
acceptance_criteria:
- Replaying the same event twice changes nothing (test)
- DLQ alarm configured

title: Write the privacy policy
description: Covers what we collect (account, team, inventory, sheets, client names, receipt photos, usage), why, how long we keep it, subprocessors (AWS including Bedrock, Stripe, email provider), that Bedrock doesn't train on customer data, receipt photos not stored by default, account deletion, data export, CCPA rights, cookies, children, contact. Needed for the site, App Store and Play listings.
acceptance_criteria:
- Published at /privacy on the marketing site and linked from sign-up and the apps
- Matches the actual retention settings in the ADRs
- Reviewed by a lawyer or a reputable policy generator plus a manual check
notes: Add RevenueCat, Apple and Google (in-app purchases) as processors (ADR 0013).

title: Send transactional email with SES: invites and notices
description: Templates for invites, trial ending, payment failed, read-only notice, export ready. Bounce and complaint handling via SNS; suppression list.
acceptance_criteria:
- Emails render on Gmail, Outlook and iOS Mail
- Bounces are suppressed automatically

title: Create GitHub Actions OIDC deploy roles for each account
description: An IAM OIDC provider for token.actions.githubusercontent.com in dev, staging and prod, with a deploy role trusting only this repo and the matching GitHub environment.
acceptance_criteria:
- A workflow in a branch assumes the dev role without stored keys
- Prod role can only be assumed from the `production` environment

title: Invite members by email with a role
description: Owner enters email and role; SES sends a link with a single-use token (hashed at rest, 7-day expiry). Accepting signs in or signs up and joins the team. Owners can resend or revoke.
acceptance_criteria:
- Invite, accept, revoke and expiry all covered by tests
- Invite links open the mobile app when installed (later: universal links)

title: Set up the support email address
description: support@<domain> into a shared inbox (for example Google Workspace group or a help desk like Help Scout), auto-reply with expected response time, and a signature linking the help center. Linked from the app, site, app stores and Stripe emails.
acceptance_criteria:
- Mail to support@ reaches both of us and gets an auto-reply
- SPF/DKIM/DMARC pass for replies

title: Set up observability: logs, metrics, traces, dashboards and alarms
description: Structured JSON logs (Powertools for Lambda), X-Ray/OpenTelemetry traces, business metrics (checkouts, receipts, signups), dashboards per region, alarms to email and SMS via SNS. Log retention per the infosec policy.
acceptance_criteria:
- Dashboard shows traffic, errors, latency and business metrics per region
- Test alarm reaches phone

title: Add automated rollbacks: Lambda canaries, alarms and web version rollback
description: CodeDeploy Canary10Percent5Minutes on every function's live alias with 5xx, latency and business-error alarms. Web release pointer rolls back automatically when post-deploy canaries fail. Stateful stacks protected. Expand/contract rule for data changes documented.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deliberately broken release in staging rolls back on its own in under 10 minutes
- Runbook documents manual rollback too

title: Runtime adapter: AWS implementation of window.claude (db, user, downloads, sample)
description: The AWS build of the interface in ADR 0004: db (collections, docs, onSnapshot, orderBy, increment), user (role from membership), downloads (browser download), sample (receipt endpoint). Plus sign-in screen, team switcher and settings shell.
acceptance_criteria:
- The app works end-to-end on dev with a real account
- Existing mock-based suites still pass
- View-only users see the existing view-only notice

title: Define subscription tiers and pricing
description: Starting proposal from ADR 0009: Starter $9/month including 3 seats, then $3 per extra seat, 200 receipts per team per month; annual plan with 2 months free; 14-day trial with no card. Decide limits per tier (seats, receipts, history kept), what a viewer seat costs (free?), and whether there is a free plan.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tier table (price, included seats, per-seat price, receipt limit, features) written into the business plan
- Receipt limits checked against the Bedrock cost per receipt
- Stripe fee share is under 10% at the smallest paid plan
notes: ADR 0013: the apps sell fixed seat bundles (store subscriptions have no quantity). Define bundle levels and store prices too, allowing for the 15% store fee plus RevenueCat's 1% above $2,500 a month tracked revenue.

title: Move the app into a Vite build that outputs the artifact and a static bundle
description: Per ADR 0004: split index.html into modules without changing behavior. `npm run build:artifact` produces the single index.html for claude.ai (as today); `npm run build:web` produces a hashed bundle for CloudFront. Existing Playwright suites run against both builds with the mock.
acceptance_criteria:
- All existing tests pass against both builds
- Artifact output works when republished to claude.ai
- README updated

title: Choose the product name and register the domain
description: Check trademark conflicts and domain availability for the product name, register the domain in Route 53 (or transfer DNS to it), and reserve matching social handles.
acceptance_criteria:
- Name chosen after a basic USPTO trademark search
- Domain registered, DNS hosted in the prod account's Route 53

title: Define the customer journeys
description: Write the journeys the product must never break, with steps and expected results: (1) visit site, sign up, start trial; (2) create team, add inventory; (3) invite crew, crew accepts on phone; (4) create sheet, check out by barcode and by hand, return, finish; (5) scan receipt, review, assign to sheet and inventory; (6) export CSV; (7) subscribe, add seats, see invoice; (8) payment fails, grace, read-only, recover; (9) viewer can see but not change; (10) cancel and export; (11) delete account.
acceptance_criteria:
- docs/journeys.md with each journey, persona, steps and expected results
- Each journey tagged with the test that covers it
notes: Add journey: owner chooses and buys a seat-bundle plan in the iOS or Android app, then restores it on a new phone (ADR 0013).

title: Make stacks multi-region-ready: region parameter, global table, team home region
description: Per ADR 0010 phasing. Every stack deploys to either region, the global table has both replicas, and teams have homeRegion from creation. MVP serves from us-east-1.
acceptance_criteria:
- Staging deploys cleanly to us-west-2 from the same pipeline
- homeRegion set on every team

title: Scaffold the CDK app with cdk-nag and the stack layout
description: infra/ npm workspace, CDK v2 TypeScript, bootstrapped in dev/staging/prod in both regions. Stacks: stateful (table, keys, user pool, buckets) separate from stateless (API, functions, CDN). cdk-nag AwsSolutions checks on synth; CDK assertion tests in CI.
acceptance_criteria:
- `npm run -w infra synth` passes with cdk-nag and no unsuppressed findings
- Stack per region takes region as a parameter
- Unit tests run in CI

title: Build the HTTP API and data Lambdas for products and sheets with team isolation
description: HTTP API with JWT authorizer; routes for products and sheets matching what the adapter needs (list, get, set, deep-merge update, delete, ordered list of sheets). Team ID comes from the path and is checked against membership; IAM LeadingKeys condition as a second layer.
acceptance_criteria:
- A user can't read or write another team's data (automated negative tests)
- p95 under 300 ms warm in dev
- OpenAPI description checked in

title: Enforce roles on the server and in the UI; add the members screen
description: Owner: everything including billing and members. Contributor: scan, edit sheets and inventory. Viewer: read-only. Members screen lists members and roles; owners change roles or remove members. At least one owner always.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every write route checks role (automated tests per role)
- Last owner can't be removed or demoted

title: Send live updates through DynamoDB Streams to per-team AppSync Events channels
description: Per ADR 0006. A stream consumer in each region publishes change events to /teams/{teamId}; a Lambda authorizer checks membership on subscribe. The adapter refetches on reconnect. Polling fallback when WebSockets are blocked.
acceptance_criteria:
- A change on one device shows on another within 2 seconds (p95) in staging
- A non-member can't subscribe to a team channel (test)
- Reconnect after 5 minutes offline shows correct data

title: Set up the Stripe account, products and prices for the tiers
description: Stripe account on the business entity, products/prices from the tier decision (monthly and annual, per-seat quantity), branding, email receipts on, test and live keys stored in Secrets Manager (replicated).
acceptance_criteria:
- Products and prices created by script (reproducible in test and live mode)
- Keys only in Secrets Manager

title: Enable Claude models in Bedrock in both regions and request quotas
description: Submit the Anthropic use-case form, enable Claude Haiku 4.5 and Claude Sonnet 5 in us-east-1 and us-west-2 in dev, staging and prod. Record the exact model IDs and whether a cross-region inference profile is needed. Request tokens-per-minute quota for expected launch volume.
acceptance_criteria:
- A test call to each model succeeds from each account and region
- Model IDs recorded in infra config

title: MVP live in AWS
description: All mvp-phase beads are done: a new customer can sign up, pay, invite crew and use every core journey in production, with CI/CD, rollbacks, backups, policies and support in place.

title: Set up AWS Budgets and cost anomaly alerts
description: Monthly budget per account with alerts at 50/80/100%, plus a cost anomaly monitor. Alerts go to email.
acceptance_criteria:
- Budgets and anomaly monitor in every account
- Test alert received

title: Build the receipt-reading Lambda on Bedrock with structured output
description: Per ADR 0008: POST /teams/{id}/receipts:read. Uses AnthropicBedrockMantle from @anthropic-ai/bedrock-sdk, the existing RECEIPT_PROMPT rules, team inventory, prompt caching and an output_config.format JSON schema matching the review screen. Model ID from config. Maps errors to the codes the app already handles (rate_limited, image_rejected, etc.).
acceptance_criteria:
- The review screen works unchanged with the Lambda's output
- No AWS credentials or model calls in the browser
- Token usage logged per call

title: Build team creation and first sign-in onboarding
description: First sign-in creates a team (the user becomes owner) or accepts a pending invite. Team name, home region (set from the region that served sign-up), trial start.
acceptance_criteria:
- New user reaches an empty team ready to add inventory in under 1 minute
- A user in two teams can switch between them

title: Set up the Route 53 zone, ACM certificates and SES domain
description: Hosted zone in prod with delegated subdomains for dev and staging; ACM certs (us-east-1 for CloudFront, both regions for APIs); SES domain identity with DKIM, SPF and DMARC in both regions; request SES production access.
acceptance_criteria:
- app., api., realtime., auth. names resolve in each environment
- SES out of sandbox in prod; DMARC report shows passing mail

title: Automate end-to-end tests for every customer journey against deployed environments
description: Playwright tests that follow each journey against a preview or staging stack, with real Cognito test users, Stripe test mode and test clocks, a stub Bedrock mode for determinism plus one real-model smoke test. Run in desktop and mobile projects.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every journey in docs/journeys.md has a passing test
- Suite runs on every staging deploy and blocks promotion on failure
- Test data cleaned up after each run

title: Set up AWS Organizations, accounts and IAM Identity Center
description: Per ADR 0003: turn the current account into the management account and create log-archive, security, dev, staging and prod accounts. An Identity Center instance already exists in us-east-1 on this account (start URL is in local notes, not this public repo). Confirm it is an organization instance, not an account instance. Create permission sets (Admin, Developer, ReadOnly) with MFA, and CLI profiles via `aws configure sso`.
acceptance_criteria:
- Organization with the 5 member accounts
- Identity Center permission sets assigned; MFA enforced
- `aws sts get-caller-identity` works with a profile for each account
- No IAM users or access keys in any account

title: Enforce subscription status with a grace period and read-only mode
description: Active/trialing: full access. Past due: banner and 7-day grace, then read-only. Canceled: read-only for 30 days with export, then deletion per the privacy policy.
acceptance_criteria: - Each status tested end to end with Stripe test clocks

title: Host the web app on S3 and CloudFront with WAF and versioned releases
description: S3 buckets in both regions (replication), CloudFront origin group, releases under /releases/<version>/, CloudFront Function selecting the live version, security headers (CSP, HSTS), AWS WAF managed rules and rate limiting.
acceptance_criteria:
- app.<domain> serves the build over HTTPS with an A grade on securityheaders.com
- Switching the live version takes under a minute

title: Build full CI/CD: PR previews, staging deploy on merge, prod on release
description: Per ADR 0012. PR: existing gates plus infra tests, cdk diff comment, preview stack in dev (deleted on close). Merge: build once, deploy staging in both regions, run journey tests. Release: promote the same artifacts to prod, us-west-2 then us-east-1, behind the production environment.
acceptance_criteria:
- A merged PR reaches staging without manual steps
- Artifacts deployed to prod are byte-for-byte the ones tested in staging
- Preview stacks are cleaned up

title: Write the terms of service and acceptable use policy
description: Subscription terms, auto-renewal and cancellation, refunds, trial, acceptable use, customer owns their data, service levels (best effort at launch), liability limits, governing law.
acceptance_criteria:
- Published at /terms, accepted with a checkbox at sign-up (acceptance time stored)
- Auto-renewal wording meets state auto-renewal laws (clear disclosure, easy cancellation)

title: Add per-team receipt limits, per-user rate limits and usage metrics
description: Monthly receipt counter per team using the tier limit; per-user rate limit; CloudWatch metrics for receipts, tokens and cost per team; alarm when any team uses more than 3x its expected cost.
acceptance_criteria:
- Over-limit returns a clear message and an upgrade link
- Usage visible to owners in settings

title: Build Stripe Checkout for sign-up and seat-based subscriptions with a 14-day trial
description: Owner picks plan and seats; server creates a Checkout Session linked to the team's Stripe customer. Trial without card; prompt for a card before the trial ends.
acceptance_criteria:
- Test-mode purchase makes the team active
- Trial expiry without a card makes the team read-only with a clear banner

title: Automate releases: release-please drives prod deploys and artifact publishing
description: Keep release-please as the version source. The release workflow deploys prod, attaches index.html for the claude.ai artifact, and (later) triggers mobile builds. Release notes list linked beads.
acceptance_criteria:
- Merging the release PR deploys prod with no other action
- Changelog and GitHub Release created

title: Review and accept ADRs 0002-0013
description: Read docs/adr and docs/architecture. Mark each ADR Accepted, change it, or reject it. Several beads assume these decisions.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every ADR has status Accepted or Superseded
- Any changed decision is reflected in the affected beads

title: Create the DynamoDB table with KMS, PITR and global table replicas
description: Single table from ADR 0005, on-demand, customer-managed KMS key, PITR, deletion protection, streams (new and old images), replicas in us-east-1 and us-west-2 from day one. Data-access module with TeamContext; lint rule banning direct DynamoDB client use elsewhere.
acceptance_criteria:
- Table deployed with both replicas in dev
- Access-pattern unit tests for every entity in ADR 0005 (DynamoDB Local)

title: Set up the Cognito user pool with Managed Login, passkeys, Apple and Google sign-in
description: Per ADR 0007. Email code/password, passkeys, Sign in with Apple, Google. Custom domain auth.<domain>, branded Managed Login. Token lifetimes per ADR. Optional MFA; required for owners before billing changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- Sign up and sign in with each method in dev
- Tokens verified by the API authorizer
- Refresh works; no tokens in localStorage

title: Web and mobile clients
description:
Supported desktop and mobile browsers, and native iOS/Android apps. ADR 0011.

See docs/adr and docs/architecture.

title: Backend platform and app adapter
description:
Data, API, live updates, sign-in and hosting, plus the runtime adapter that lets the existing app run on them. ADR 0004-0007.

See docs/adr and docs/architecture.

title: Turn on Stripe Tax and register where required
description: Decide where we must collect sales tax on SaaS, register, and turn on Stripe Tax with the right product tax code.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tax calculated on test invoices for a taxable state
- Registrations recorded

title: Make stock increments atomic and writes versioned
description: Replace read-then-write `bumpStock` with a server-side ADD. Add a version number to products and sheets; conditional updates return 409 on conflict and the UI refreshes that line.
acceptance_criteria:
- Two parallel checkouts of the same item never lose a count (test)
- A conflicting edit shows a clear message and the latest values

title: Support and operations
description:
Support email, transactional email, observability and runbooks.

See docs/adr and docs/architecture.

title: Run a pilot with the family business and 3-5 teams
description: Move the family business off the artifact first, then invite a few friendly crews on free plans. Weekly feedback.
acceptance_criteria:
- At least 3 teams using it weekly for 2 weeks
- Feedback triaged into beads

title: AWS foundation
description:
Accounts, identity, guardrails, DNS and model access that every other epic builds on. ADR 0002, 0003.

See docs/adr and docs/architecture.

title: Build a receipt eval set and choose the model
description: Collect 30-50 real receipts (crumpled, faded, long, multiple stores) with hand-checked expected line items. Score Haiku 4.5 and Sonnet 5 on line items, quantities, unit prices and inventory matches, plus cost and latency per receipt.
acceptance_criteria:
- Eval script and labeled set (photos kept private, not in this public repo)
- Results table and chosen model recorded in ADR 0008

title: Write the information security policy
description: Access control (Identity Center, MFA, least privilege, break-glass), encryption at rest and in transit, logging and monitoring, vulnerability and patch management (Dependabot, npm audit, CodeQL), secure development (PR review, CI gates), backups and recovery, vendor management, incident response, employee onboarding and offboarding. Written so it can grow into SOC 2 later.
acceptance_criteria:
- docs/security/information-security-policy.md
- Each control maps to a real setting or process (link the bead or config)
- Review date set for 12 months out

title: Resize receipt photos on the device before upload
description: Shrink to at most 1568 px on the long edge, JPEG about 0.8 quality, fix EXIF rotation. Keeps requests under Lambda's 6 MB limit and reduces tokens.
acceptance_criteria:
- A 12 MP phone photo uploads as under 600 KB
- Rotated photos read correctly

title: Teams, roles and accounts
description:
Multi-tenant teams with owner/contributor/viewer roles, invites, export and account deletion. ADR 0005, 0007.

See docs/adr and docs/architecture.

title: Resilience and multi-region
description:
Backups, multi-region readiness, and active-active with automatic regional failover. ADR 0010.

See docs/adr and docs/architecture.

title: Billing, invoices and payments
description:
Stripe subscriptions, invoices, one-time and scheduled payments, and access rules. ADR 0009.

See docs/adr and docs/architecture.

title: Set up backups: PITR, AWS Backup to a separate account and a restore drill
description: PITR on the table, AWS Backup daily copies to the log-archive (or backup) account with vault lock, S3 versioning. Restore drill into staging.
acceptance_criteria: - Restore drill done and time to restore recorded

title: Forward writes to the team's home region and take over when it fails
description: Writes arriving in the non-home region are forwarded; if the home region is unhealthy, the other region takes over and updates homeRegion. Avoids last-writer-wins conflicts on counters.
acceptance_criteria: - Concurrent checkouts from both regions never lose stock counts (test)

title: Run adapter contract tests against a real staging API
description: The same contract suite runs against mock-claude.js and the AWS adapter, so the mock can't drift from reality (merge semantics, ordering, onSnapshot timing, errors).
acceptance_criteria: - Contract suite passes against both implementations

title: Launch
description:
Landing page, sign-up, pilot and the launch readiness review.

See docs/adr and docs/architecture.

title: Report front-end errors with CloudWatch RUM
description: Capture JS errors and page performance from real users without collecting personal data.
acceptance_criteria: - Errors from the app appear in RUM with release version

title: Set up the business entity, bank account and D-U-N-S number
description: Stripe, Apple's organization developer account, Google Play and sales tax registration all need a legal business with a bank account. Apple needs a D-U-N-S number, which can take a couple of weeks.
acceptance_criteria:
- Entity formed (or existing one chosen) and EIN on file
- Business bank account open
- D-U-N-S number issued

title: Support mobile web on all major browsers and screen sizes
description: iOS Safari, Chrome on Android, Samsung Internet and Firefox Android. Widths 320-430 px phones, tablets, portrait and landscape. Add Playwright device projects (Pixel, Galaxy, iPad) and a real-device check (BrowserStack or similar) before each release.
acceptance_criteria:
- No sideways scrolling at 320, 360, 390, 430 and 768 px
- Camera and barcode scanning checked on a real iPhone and Android phone

title: Add self-serve account deletion and team closure
description: Required by the App Store and promised in the privacy policy. Deleting an account removes the Cognito user and personal data; an owner must pass ownership or close the team (which cancels the subscription and schedules data deletion after 30 days).
acceptance_criteria:
- Deletion completes without contacting support
- Data is gone from the table after the stated period (checked by test)

title: Add automatic regional failover (active-active) for the API and live updates
description: Second region's HTTP API and AppSync Events live in prod; Route 53 latency routing with health checks on /health; CloudFront origin failover for the web app.
acceptance_criteria:
- Failing us-east-1's health check moves traffic to us-west-2 within 2 minutes in staging
- Journey tests pass against each region directly

title: Write the incident response and breach notification plan
description: Severity levels, who is paged, first-hour checklist, customer communication templates, and state breach-notification deadlines.
acceptance_criteria:
- docs/security/incident-response.md
- One tabletop exercise done and notes recorded

title: Turn on CloudTrail, GuardDuty, Security Hub, Config and SCPs
description: Organization CloudTrail to log-archive with Object Lock; GuardDuty and Security Hub delegated to the security account; SCPs deny leaving the org, disabling logging, and regions other than us-east-1/us-west-2.
acceptance_criteria:
- Findings from all accounts visible in the security account
- SCP blocks creating a resource in eu-west-1 (tested)

title: Show invoices in the app and email them
description: Stripe emails invoices and receipts; the billing screen lists past invoices with hosted and PDF links; company name, address and tax ID fields on invoices.
acceptance_criteria:
- Invoice list matches Stripe
- Invoice PDF shows the team's billing details

title: Receipt reading on Bedrock
description:
Move receipt reading from claude.ai sampling to a Lambda calling Claude on Amazon Bedrock. ADR 0008.

See docs/adr and docs/architecture.

title: Write the business plan
description: Target customers (cleaning, maintenance, contractor and property crews who take supplies to client jobs), the problem, competitors, pricing, go-to-market, a 24-month revenue and cost model, and risks. Cost model covers AWS fixed costs per environment, per-user AWS and Bedrock costs (ADR 0008 has per-receipt estimates), Stripe fees (2.9% + $0.30 per charge), app store fees and tooling. Show break-even in paying seats.
acceptance_criteria:
- docs/business-plan.md (or a private doc) covering all sections above
- Cost model spreadsheet with per-seat margin at 1, 3, 10 and 50 seats per team
- Break-even point stated
notes: Model margin separately for web (Stripe) and store (App Store / Google Play + RevenueCat) billed teams, and an assumed mix between them.

title: Keep the seat quantity in sync with team members
description: Adding or removing a paid member updates the subscription quantity with proration. Decide whether viewers count as seats (biz-tiers).
acceptance_criteria: - Seat count always equals billable members (nightly reconciliation job alerts on drift)

title: Security review before launch
description: Review tenant isolation, auth, webhooks, uploads and headers against OWASP ASVS level 1; fix findings; consider an external pentest once revenue allows.
acceptance_criteria: - Findings tracked as beads; no high or critical open at launch

title: Run a region failover game day with journey tests
description: Quarterly and before announcing active-active: fail a region in staging and run the journey suite.
acceptance_criteria: - Game day report with RTO/RPO measured against ADR 0010 targets

title: CI/CD, releases and rollbacks
description:
Every merge reaches production through staging, with canaries and automatic rollback. ADR 0012.

See docs/adr and docs/architecture.

title: Run CloudWatch Synthetics canaries for core journeys in prod
description: Sign in, open a sheet, check out and return a test item on a dedicated test team, in each region every 5-15 minutes. Alarms feed rollback and paging.
acceptance_criteria: - Canaries green in prod; failing canary alerts within 10 minutes

title: Support all major desktop browsers
description: Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari, current and previous major versions. Add Playwright projects for Firefox, desktop WebKit and branded Edge; set a browserslist target; fix what breaks.
acceptance_criteria:
- All suites (app, a11y, layout, resilience) pass in the 4 desktop browsers in CI
- Supported browsers listed in the help center

title: Quality and customer-journey testing
description:
Defined customer journeys, automated end-to-end tests for each, and production canaries.

See docs/adr and docs/architecture.

title: Write runbooks for rollback, region failover and dependency outages
description: Manual rollback, region evacuation, Stripe outage, Bedrock outage or quota exhaustion, SES suspension, leaked secret rotation.
acceptance_criteria: - docs/runbooks/ with one page per scenario, each rehearsed once in staging

title: Business, legal and pricing
description:
Everything the business needs before it can take money: plan, entity, pricing, policies and terms.

See docs/adr and docs/architecture.

title: Add security scanning to CI: CodeQL, secret scanning, SBOM and dependency review
description: CodeQL for JS/TS, GitHub secret scanning and push protection, SBOM on release, dependency review already exists (keep), cdk-nag in the infra job.
acceptance_criteria:
- All scanners required for merge
- SBOM attached to each release

title: Export all team data as CSV and JSON
description: Owners can download all sheets and inventory at any time, including after cancellation during the read-only period.
acceptance_criteria:
- Export matches what the app shows
- Works for a team with 1,000 sheets in under 30 seconds

title: Test store purchases automatically and on real devices
description: StoreKit configuration file tests in CI (iOS simulator), Google Play license testers, sandbox renewals, billing retry, refunds and upgrades between bundles. Run before each mobile release.
acceptance_criteria:
- The 'subscribe in the app' journey has automated coverage on both platforms
- Real-device sandbox purchase checked before each store release

title: Add the in-app plan picker and purchase flow with RevenueCat
description: Owners only: Plans screen in the iOS and Android apps with seat bundles, monthly or annual, price, period, trial terms, and links to terms and privacy (App Store 3.1.2). Purchase through @revenuecat/purchases-capacitor, Restore Purchases, and a link to manage the subscription in iOS Settings or the Play Store. Non-owners see 'Ask your team owner to upgrade'. Teams billed elsewhere see where to manage their plan.
acceptance_criteria:
- Sandbox purchase on iOS and Android activates the team within a minute
- Restore Purchases works on a reinstalled app
- Purchase screen passes App Review checklist for subscriptions

title: Enforce one billing source per team and the store-to-web switch
description: A team can have only one active billing source. Web Checkout is blocked while a store subscription is active and vice versa. Switching from store to web: guide the owner to cancel in the store; web billing starts at the end of the store period. Handles Apple's one-subscription-per-group limit (an owner of two teams can buy only one with the same Apple ID).
acceptance_criteria:
- No path in web or app creates a second active subscription for a team (tests)
- Switching from store to web tested end to end with sandbox and Stripe test clocks

title: Process RevenueCat webhooks into team entitlements
description: Per ADR 0013. Webhook endpoint in both regions: check the authorization header, store the event ID for idempotency (WEBHOOK#revenuecat#id), queue on SQS, worker sets billingSource (app_store or play), plan, seatLimit, status and periodEnd. Handles purchase, renewal, cancellation, billing issue, expiration, refund and product change.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each event type tested with RevenueCat sandbox events
- Replayed events change nothing
- Store refunds make the team read-only under the same rules as Stripe

title: Create App Store and Google Play subscription products (seat bundles)
